symbols.doc: The deterministic rubrics are real gates now, not a report.
symbols.name: test_a_blocking_review_finding_blocks_the_close

symbols.doc:
A reviewer agent's own blocking finding must stop the close too —
    otherwise recording it changes nothing.
symbols.name: test_agent_recorded_findings_are_surfaced_at_close

symbols.doc:
The close message promises: 'agent-recorded blockers clear by
    recording the fix'. A LATER record with the same code and a non-block
    severity is that fix — the close must proceed (last record per code
    wins; edges are append-only).
symbols.name: test_a_recorded_fix_clears_an_agent_blocking_finding

symbols.doc: Ordering is honest both ways: block -> fix -> re-block still blocks.
symbols.name: test_a_reblock_after_a_fix_blocks_again

symbols.doc:
Parking is the reviewer saying 'a human must rule on this' — closing
    over it would make parking meaningless.
symbols.name: test_an_unadjudicated_park_blocks_the_close

symbols.doc:
`g5_override: recorded_justification` is a first-class resolution: an
    undeclared use with a recorded override passes the close's own
    uses ⊆ declares check, so the Layer-1 R-uses rubric must read the same
    override-aware set (`unresolved`), not `undeclared` — otherwise the
    override clears the gate and the review blocks the close anyway.
symbols.name: test_a_recorded_g5_override_satisfies_r_uses
